title: Unit file footprint (units/<Uxx>/footprint.json)
description: 1.15.0 (blast radius). The FILE footprint of one unit: the repository paths that actually changed while the unit ran, captured by scripts/footprint.py from two workspace snapshots (or two tree-ishes) and written next to a footprint.json.sha256 sidecar in `shasum -a 256` format (`<hex>  footprint.json`). NOT the TOKEN footprint: debrief.json's required `footprint` object ({tokens_consumed, within_budget}) is an unrelated token-usage report that only shares the word. Field contract (restated here so the schema is self-describing): `mode` is how the capture was taken — 'git' (content-addressed tree ids of the workspace minus excludes), 'snapshot' (no git: per-file sha256 entries plus a write-once content store under the run directory), 'none' (no capture mechanism available). `base_ref` is what BEFORE content is read from: the PRE tree id in git wave mode, the pre tree-ish exactly as given in tree mode, null in snapshot mode. `pre_snapshot_sha256`/`post_snapshot_sha256` are the sha256 of the two snapshot files the capture compared, null in tree mode (no snapshot files). `changes[]` is the content diff between the two states: status A (added), M (modified), D (deleted), R (renamed: `path` is the new path, `from_path` the old one), T (type change); `sha256_before`/`sha256_after` are the sha256 of the path's bytes before/after, null when the path is absent on that side. `unattributed[]` lists changed paths that no unit of the capturing wave claims through its frame.modifies patterns (recorded in every footprint that capture writes). FAIL-CLOSED: any capture error (git error, timeout, unsafe path, unreadable snapshot) sets `capture_error` to a one-line reason and `changes` to [] — never a partial list; a clean capture has `capture_error: null`. `tool_version` names the writer (e.g. 'footprint.py/<ver>'). Every object is closed.

iteration.description: The unit iteration this capture belongs to (debrief.json.iteration of the unit; 1 when no debrief exists yet). A retry re-captures and rewrites the footprint for its own iteration.

base_ref.description: Where BEFORE content is read from: the PRE tree id (git wave mode), the pre tree-ish as given (tree mode), null (snapshot mode — BEFORE bytes come from the content store keyed by sha256_before).

path.description: POSIX path relative to the workspace root (the NEW path for a rename).

from_path.description: The OLD path of a rename (status R); null for every other status.

allOf.$comment: A rename carries its old path; nothing else does.
An added path has no BEFORE bytes.
A deleted path has no AFTER bytes.

capture_error.description: null on a clean capture; otherwise a one-line reason, and then `changes` MUST be [] (enforced by the allOf below).

allOf.$comment: Fail-closed capture: an errored capture records NO change list, never a partial one.
Snapshot mode has no git object to read BEFORE content from.
